ceiling_statement: Under the declared operating model (single node, fair scheduler, eventually-available storage, finite committed inputs, external calls that may fail forever), the maximum achievable liveness is CONDITIONAL BOUNDED TERMINATION: every admitted task reaches, within an explicit per-task budget B(task), exactly one of three terminal states — SUCCESS with certificate, typed FAIL, or typed UNKNOWN/REFUSED — with no livelock, no unbounded retry, and no silent hang; retries are idempotent so a re-attempt after partial failure has exactly-once observable effect on committed state; after a crash, work resumes from the last checkpoint with bounded re-execution. Unconditional liveness (progress no matter what the environment does) is UNACHIEVABLE by any system honoring H3 — blocking on persistent environment misbehavior is forced, and the ceiling converts every such block into a typed, bounded-time refusal rather than a hang.
derivation: Three impossibility facts pin the ceiling. (1) Fail-closed vs. progress trade-off: H3 requires blocking on error/violation/unknown; an adversarial environment (storage returning EIO forever, origin never serving valid bytes) can therefore stall any H3-compliant system indefinitely — so 'progress' can only ever be conditional on declared environment assumptions; the maximum is making the condition explicit and the failure mode a bounded-time typed refusal (H2) instead of a hang. This is the single-node analogue of FLP: safety-preserving systems buy liveness only from environment assumptions. (2) Exactly-once effects: at-least-once retry plus at-most-once effect is achievable only via idempotence/deduplication state — exactly-once delivery without a dedup record is classically impossible — so idempotency-keyed retries checked against a durable journal are the ceiling mechanism, not an option; without them retries violate H6 all-or-nothing. (3) Termination cannot be inferred: by Rice/halting, a system cannot decide termination of arbitrary loops, so the maximum feasible guarantee is termination BY CONSTRUCTION — every trusted loop carries a well-founded variant (strictly decreasing measure or finite budget), making non-termination structurally impossible rather than tested-for. Bounded recovery follows from AX-15's checkpoint bound.
attainment_mechanism: B0 already holds the seat pattern: source/autonomy.lisp bounds consecutive errors (verified max-consecutive-errors, lines 34–45, enforcement at line 101) and checkpoints the agenda for resume; authority-v2/run-proofs.sh terminates in deterministic fail-closed exit codes; systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/frbr-conditions.lisp gives typed abort conditions; source/circuit-breaker.lisp bounds external-call retry. Ceiling attainment: (1) give every executor stage (systems/orchestrator-core/executor.lisp) a declared step/retry budget and a variant function — agenda strictly shrinks or budget strictly decrements each iteration, so infinite loops cannot be written; (2) idempotency keys: retryKey = SHA-256(stage-id, committed-input hashes) recorded in the durable journal (AX-15 seat, source/journal.lisp) before effects, checked on re-entry — re-execution is skip-or-byte-identical; (3) budget exhaustion raises a typed condition from frbr-conditions.lisp that propagates to a REFUSED terminal state (never marked-executed); (4) circuit-breaker timeouts driven by the logical clock seat (systems/orchestrator-ai-core/config.lisp) so liveness decisions replay under H5. All SBCL, buildable today.
b0_gap: Per B0 map: executor retry is NOT idempotency-checked (systems/orchestrator-core/executor.lisp) — a retry after partial effect can double-apply; systems/orchestrator-core/parallel-executor.lisp marks failed stages executed (handler-case → nil, verified lines 71–81, 116–122) — today's 'liveness' is bought by silently discarding failures, which is fail-open and violates H3, the opposite of the ceiling's typed-refusal terminal; source/circuit-breaker.lisp uses :system wall-clock so retry/abort decisions are not replayable (H5 break); no global termination variant exists — boundedness is per-mission convention (autonomy.lisp) rather than a structural property of every trusted loop; omega use-default restarts (frbr-conditions.lisp) convert failures into synthesized content instead of typed refusal (B0 map §3 AX-10 residual).
lean_obligation: Theorem (conditional bounded termination): define the executor as a labelled transition system with state (agenda, journal, budgets) and an environment oracle E. (1) Termination: exhibit μ : State → ℕ with ∀ s s', Step s s' → μ s' < μ s; conclude by well-founded induction that every run reaches a terminal state in ≤ μ s₀ steps, terminal : Terminal := Success cert | Fail reason | Refused reason (the type has no 'hang' inhabitant). (2) Conditional progress: under hypothesis Fair E ∧ Avail E, the terminal state of an admitted task is Success cert. (3) Retry idempotence: ∀ s, committedEffects (exec (exec s)) = committedEffects (exec s), proved from the journal-key check. (4) No silent degradation: ∀ stage failure, resulting terminal ≠ Success — i.e., markExecuted is only reachable from a stage-success derivation (making the parallel-executor bug unrepresentable).
